data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

94% of stocks in the S&P 500 declined for the week, 11 of them by at least 20%. But for now, analysts still think you can make a lot of money if you buy them.

Nvidia's stock declined nearly 14% on Nov. 20. It was down almost 23% for the week and more than 38% since the end of October.

The stock market's technology-led correction accelerated on Friday, but a quick look at consensus price targets shows that Wall Street analysts still expected great things from the week's biggest decliners - for now.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA declined 1.9% on Friday, while the S&P 500 SPX was down 3.7% and the Nasdaq Composite COMP fell 5.3%. Drilling further, the S&P 500's information-technology sector XX:SP500.45 plunged 7.1% for the session.

A quick look at the week's declines for the sectors of the S&P 500 shows that the pain was widespread, but that the IT sector took the hardest hit. That was followed by the communications-services sector, which includes Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META); together, those stocks make up 39.3% of the State Street SPDR Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF XLC.

data.title: Chip stocks see $2.3 trillion weekly wipeout as panic grips the AI trade
data.description:
By William Gavin

A major semiconductor index just posted its worst weekly performance in 25 years

Semiconductor companies have been hit hard in recent trading.

The chip sector's worst week in a quarter-century saw $2.3 trillion in market capitalization evaporate.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX plunged 10.7% on Friday, erasing $1.3 trillion in market cap in a single session, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That decline helped carry the index to its worst weekly performance since Sept. 21, 2001, according to Dow Jones Market Data. It fell 17.1% this week.

All 30 stocks in the index were down by at least 5% or more on Friday, with the day's biggest losers including Astera Labs (ALAB), Credo Technology (CRDO) and Arm (ARM). Each of those stocks were down between 14% and 16%.

The first half of 2026 was marked by "over-exuberance, speculation, greed, complacency," Ted Mortonson, a managing director at Baird, told MarketWatch on Thursday. Since this month began, the market has turned to "fear" and "panic," he said.

Earlier concerns about the "AI bubble" have been amplified in recent days, despite strong earnings from Nvidia (NVDA) this week. The company is hunting for a successor to former CEO Jensen Huang, and Nvidia is facing greater scrutiny from the U.S. government.

Losses at Nvidia were steep enough to send its market valuation to $3.03 trillion, putting the company below Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) for the first time in two years. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares fell 13% on Friday, extending sharp declines from Thursday when a short-seller report discussed whether its chips had made their way to Chinese servers. AMD has called the report inaccurate.

Shares of both Nvidia and AMD have also been impacted by new restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips. Furthermore, the Federal Communications Commission is considering restrictions on optical equipment.

Proposed bills in Congress that would limit chip and chip-equipment exports are gaining popularity as well, according to Raymond James analyst Ed Mills, who called such rules a "growing headwind for the tech industry."

"Our base case is that this is likely the beginning of a more restrictive phase in technology export controls and AI-model access vis-à-vis China, increasing policy and market volatility in the semiconductor and AI space," Mills said in a client note on Thursday.

Some experts hoped that the pressure on chip stocks, and the overall AI trade, could be lessened by Anthropic (ANT), which went public on Thursday. But the company's initial public offering was unable to turn the tide of investor sentiment.

Anthropic shares dropped 8.5% to close at $88.91 a share on Friday, just a few dollars above their $83 IPO price.

"Investors will be nervous that we are seeing the long-feared AI bubble-burst moment unfolding," Samuel Kerr, head of global ECM at Mergermarket, earlier told MarketWatch. "If that is the case, Anthropic and other AI-linked stocks could have further to go."

-William Gavin

data.title: APEX FTE Expo 2026 Unites Aviation Leaders in Singapore and Honors Passenger Experience Excellence
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov 21, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - APEX FTE EXPO 2026 brought together nearly 2,000 registered airline, airport, and industry leaders at Marina Bay Sands Expo & Convention Centre, bringing APEX's flagship show back to Singapore for the first time in a decade as the largest end-to-end passenger experience and innovation expo, spanning every stage of the passenger journey. Hosted by the Airline Passenger Experience Association (APEX), Future Travel Experience (FTE), and the International Flight Services Association (IFSA), the EXPO united over 300 airline representatives from more than 60 airlines worldwide, airport operators, and more than 100 exhibitors under one roof, building on 15 years of APEX FTE's Asia event. The two days culminated in the APEX Awards Ceremony, where the industry honored the leaders, airlines, and innovators whose work passengers feel long after they land.

Across two days of airline chief executive keynotes, exclusive announcements, live culinary showcases, and three award ceremonies, the EXPO followed the passenger from curb to cabin, from airport technology and digital identity to inflight connectivity, cabin design, and onboard hospitality. Changi Airport Group, steward of one of the world's most celebrated airports, joined as Headline Partner, with Executive Vice President of Airport Management Jayson Goh delivering the opening keynote following welcome addresses from APEX Group CEO Dr. Joe Leader and Future Travel Experience Managing Director Max Gosney.

"Passengers remember a journey by how it felt, from the first step into the terminal to the last bite of a meal at altitude. The airlines, airports, and partners who cultivate every step of the journey with care earn the loyalty that follows," APEX Group CEO Dr. Joe Leader emphasized. "With APEX's flagship show back in Singapore for the first time in a decade, the people behind the terminal, the cabin, the connection, and the table came together in Singapore to shape the end-to-end journey. The industry that we all craft together stands as one that treats the passenger's entire trip as the turnkey product and measures itself by how it moves from the curb to the cabin to home again."

Leaders Across the Passenger Experience

The speaking lineup brought together airline and airport executives, digital innovators, technology and media leaders, and company founders and principals:

Airline Leadership

Aeromexico CEO Dr. Andres Conesa Labastida; Fiji Airways Managing Director and CEO Paul Scurrah AM; Royal Brunei Airlines INT. CEO Colonel Norsuriati binti Haji Sharbini; Oman Air CEO Nasser Al Sharji; Philippine Airlines President Richard Nuttall; Royal Brunei Airlines Chief Commercial Officer Joshua Kok Hwa Law; Air France Executive Vice President of Customer Experience Fabien Pelous; American Airlines Senior Vice President of Customer Experience Design and Strategy Rhonda Crawford; ZIPAIR Executive Officer and Chief Marketing Officer for Strategy Takuya Matsuo.

Digital, AI, and Innovation Leadership

Aeromexico Chief Digital and Customer Experience Officer Andres Castaneda; Changi Airport Group Senior Vice President of DIVA Digital Factory Jeffrey Loke; SimpliFlying Chief Product Officer Shubhodeep Pal; Axinom CEO Ralph Wagner; Pattern Labs CEO and Co-Founder Kellen Schroeter; Loyalty Status Co CEO Mark Ross-Smith; VIBEQUEST Founder and CEO Brandon Capps; Bytes not Bricks Founder Javed Malik.

Airport Leadership

Changi Airport Group Executive Vice President of Airport Management Jayson Goh; Queensland Airports Ltd. Chief of Aviation Adam Rowe.

Inflight Technology, Entertainment, and Media Leadership

Hughes Senior Vice President and General Manager Reza Rasoulian; BBC Studios Senior Vice President of Out of Home and BBC News Commercial Development for Global Markets Zina Neophytou; Spafax Senior Vice President of Global Business Development Dimitrios Tsirangelos; Sam Chui Aviation Media Consultancy Founder and Principal Sam Chui.

Design, Hospitality, and Industry Services Leadership

Tangerine Founder and Chairman Martin Darbyshire; Malaysia Aviation Group Catering Operations CEO Sagar Sanjay Dighe; dnata Catering & Retail Chief Commercial Officer for Australia and Southeast Asia Mark Stubbings; SimpliFlying Founder & CEO Shashank Nigam; JCConsulting CEO Jeremy Clark; Dooks Capital Founder and Managing Partner Peter Bellew; Threedot Founder and Managing Director Eric Leopold; Engine Managing Partner James Samperi; Hote Advisory Founder and Principal Vassilios Georgakopoulos.

Airline CEOs and Presidents Took the Stage

Airline CEOs and presidents took the APEX Premium Conference Stage to share their visions for the passenger experience, with BBC News presenter Ben Thompson moderating:

Aeromexico CEO Dr. Andres Conesa Labastida and SkyTeam Chairman

Fiji Airways Managing Director and CEO Paul Scurrah AM

Oman Air CEO Nasser Al Sharji

Philippine Airlines President Richard Nuttall

The opening "State of the Industry" panel, featuring Changi Airport Group, Royal Brunei Airlines, the National University of Singapore, and aviation media leader Sam Chui, set the tone with a look at autonomous airport technology, LEO connectivity, and bring-your-own-device entertainment.

APEX Premium Conference Stage Turned the Cabin into a Growth Engine

APEX sessions explored how the cabin is evolving into an intelligent, connected, and commercially powerful space. Highlights included:

Inflight Focus: From Inflight Entertainment to Intelligent Engagement, including an APEX exclusive on the BBC Studios streaming platform with BBC Studios, Panasonic Avionics, and Delta Air Lines

The Cabin as a Growth Engine, with Delta Air Lines, Spafax, and Thales Inflyt Experience

Winning the Network Advantage, on multi-orbit connectivity with Aeromexico, Royal Brunei Airlines, Telesat, and Viasat

On the EXPO Stage, the "Blueprint for Next-Gen Cabin Design" session gathered Airbus, Tangerine, Garuda Indonesia, AirBorneo Airways, and Delta Air Lines, while "From AI to ROI" and the CX Leaders Summit brought Etihad Airways, Star Alliance, Azerbaijan Airlines, Aeromexico, and a former Air Canada executive together to connect artificial intelligence and human service with measurable results.

FTE Advanced Smarter, More Seamless Airports

The FTE Premium Conference Stage showcased the innovations reshaping the ground journey across Asia-Pacific and beyond. Changi Airport Group revealed its work on autonomous vehicles and Terminal X, Airport Authority Hong Kong shared how Hong Kong International Airport became the first airport to achieve IATA One ID certification, and Cathay Pacific detailed innovation across customer experience, airport operations, and staff empowerment. FTE also celebrated airline and airport innovators at the FTE APAC Pioneer Awards & Hall of Fame 2026 Ceremony.

IFSA Showcased the Art of Exceptional Service

IFSA programming placed hospitality at the heart of the passenger experience. In "The Value of Hospitality: Aviation's Greatest Asset?," JCConsulting, dnata, Air New Zealand, and Loyalty Status Co examined how airlines can measure the true worth of service. "Does Ownership Matter?" brought together Malaysia Aviation Group and American Airlines to weigh in-house, partner, and hybrid models for onboard delivery.

Attendees savored the flavors of Singapore as the dnata culinary team prepared Dry Laksa and Ondeh Ondeh during the IFSA dnata Singapore Chef Showcase, while AMI Group led an IFSA wine tasting exploring the art of pairing wine with onboard dining.

Connections That Drive Business

Beyond the stages, the Speed Networking Forum connected suppliers with airline and airport buyers, while guided Tech & Innovation Tours spotlighted exhibitors across inflight services, airport technology, connectivity, and cabin design.

APEX Best(TM) Regional Awards Honored Airlines Across Asia and the South Pacific

Ahead of the evening's main ceremony, the APEX Best(TM) Awards Ceremony for Regional Awards honored airlines across Northeast Asia, Southeast Asia, Central/Southern Asia, Greater China, and the South Pacific, based on certified passenger feedback. Read the full list of regional winners here.

A Grand Finale in Singapore: The APEX Awards Ceremony

The EXPO closed with the APEX Awards Ceremony at Swissotel The Stamford, sponsored by Thales and Spafax. Airline chief executives, passenger experience leaders, and industry partners from across the globe gathered for an evening of recognition spanning lifetime achievement, passenger-rated airlines, and ideas that connect the cabin to the wider journey.

"Every honor presented in Singapore tonight traces back to a single question: what makes a journey better for the people onboard? The airlines and leaders recognized this evening answered that question with vision, discipline, and genuine care, and passengers noticed," APEX Group CEO Dr. Joe Leader commended. "From the leaders whose careers shaped our industry to the airlines that travelers themselves elevated through their ratings, tonight's honorees show what a better journey looks like. Here in Asia's growing aviation market, the global airline community comes together to celebrate them."

The ceremony recognized the following honorees and winners:

2026 APEX CEO Lifetime Achievement Award

Aeromexico CEO Dr. Andres Conesa Labastida received the 2026 APEX CEO Lifetime Achievement Award, becoming the first Latin American airline CEO to earn the honor in APEX's five-decade history. Since becoming CEO in 2005, Dr. Conesa has guided Aeromexico through industry upheaval, a global pandemic, and a successful financial restructuring, building Mexico's global airline into a benchmark for reliability and a distinctly Mexican spirit of service. Under his leadership, Cirium named Aeromexico the world's most on-time global airline in 2024 and 2025. He joins a distinguished circle of honorees that includes Air France-KLM Group CEO Benjamin Smith and United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby. Read the full press release here.

2026 APEX Lifetime Achievement Awards

APEX presented two 2026 APEX Lifetime Achievement Awards to leaders whose careers have shaped what passengers experience in flight:

Spafax Chief Executive Officer Niall McBain: Across nearly three decades as CEO, McBain transformed Spafax from a traditional inflight content provider into a global entertainment, creative, and media agency reaching nearly a billion passengers. A longtime champion of APEX, he helped sustain the association through the darkest days of the pandemic. Read the full press release here.

Terry Steiner International Founder and President Terry Steiner: For more than three decades, Steiner has built the trusted bridge between Hollywood, independent film, and the world's airlines, championing independent cinema onboard and helping airlines curate entertainment that reflects their brands. Read the full press release here.

2027 APEX Five Star(TM) and APEX Four Star(TM) Airline Awards

APEX Official Airline Ratings(TM) constitute the first airline rating program based solely on certified passenger feedback, with ratings collected via TripIt by SAP Concur across more than one million passenger-rated flights. This year, airlines around the world earned 2027 APEX Five Star(TM) and APEX Four Star(TM) recognition. Each distinction was earned entirely through the voices of the airlines' own passengers.

Click here for the full list of 2027 APEX Five Star(TM) and APEX Four Star(TM) Airline Award recipients.

2027 APEX Best(TM) Global Awards

For more than a decade, the APEX Passenger Choice Awards have recognized airline performance based entirely on verified passenger feedback. Determined by certified passenger ratings collected via TripIt by SAP Concur, the 2027 APEX Best(TM) Global Awards honor the airlines travelers rated highest in the world across five categories:

Best Cabin Service: Cathay Pacific

Best Entertainment: Emirates

Best Food & Beverage*: Turkish Airlines

Best Seat Comfort: Korean Air

Best Wi-Fi: Qatar Airways

*Best Food & Beverage Awards are presented in conjunction with the International Flight Services Association (IFSA).

Click here for the full list of 2027 APEX Best(TM) Award winners.

APEX Innovation Awards

Debuting this year, the APEX Innovation Awards celebrate the ideas making travel easier to navigate, more connected, and more human, honoring the airlines and partners putting new solutions in passengers' hands on the ground and in the air. Among this year's honors, the APEX Cabin Innovation Award recognizes work that brings design, technology, and hospitality together in the onboard environment. The 2027 APEX Innovation Award winners include:

Inflight Connectivity: Emirates

Inflight Entertainment: Thales

Safety Video: Philippine Airlines

APEX/IFSA Cabin Innovation Award: Air France

APEX World Class(TM)

APEX World Class(TM) represents the pinnacle of airline recognition, honoring carriers that deliver excellence across safety and well-being, sustainability, guest service, and food and beverage execution. These airlines were recognized for passenger experience that meets the APEX World Class(TM) standard: ANA, Emirates, Fiji Airways, Japan Airlines, Oman Air, Qatar Airways, SAUDIA, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, and Xiamen Airlines.

APEX/Crystal Cabin Award "Seamless Journey"

Uniting two of aviation's most respected recognition programs, APEX and the Crystal Cabin Award Association celebrated the first APEX/Crystal Cabin Award "Seamless Journey," bringing the Crystal Cabin Award to Asia for the first time. The award honors visionary concepts that break down the boundaries between the aircraft cabin and the wider travel experience, connecting time onboard with the airport, the transfer, the destination, and beyond. The inaugural honor was presented to Air India for its Vista Digital Platform.

"The first APEX/Crystal Cabin Award Seamless Journey carried two reputations to Asia at once: Hamburg's rigor on the cabin and APEX's view of everything around it," APEX Group CEO Dr. Joe Leader reflected. "Air India's win shows that the best ideas now start from the passenger's whole trip, then work back to the seat. Judging that idea took two organizations willing to look beyond their own borders, and Singapore was the right stage for it."

Together, the conversations and celebrations of APEX FTE EXPO 2026 left an industry united behind a single ambition: making every journey better for every passenger. The industry reconvenes next in Seoul on 3-4 November 2027. For more information on the APEX Awards Ceremony and photos of all the honors presented, please visit apex.aero.

For a full list of upcoming APEX, IFSA, and FTE events, please visit APEX Events. For more information about APEX, visit apex.aero, sign up for the APEX Daily Experience e-newsletter, or follow APEX on X, Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn.

About the Airline Passenger Experience Association (APEX)

As a global non-profit and one of the world's largest international airline associations, APEX accelerates the industry with the backing of nearly every major airline and valued supplier. APEX reinvests all its resources in serving its members, strengthening the worldwide airline industry, advancing thought-leadership, fostering business opportunities via events, developing global initiatives, setting key airline standards, and highlighting well-deserved recognition across our industry. Since 2010, the APEX Passenger Choice Awards have honored airlines based solely on verified passenger feedback, delivering transparent recognition that travelers can trust. In conjunction with both the International Flight Services Association (IFSA) and Future Travel Experience (FTE), APEX serves the full spectrum of the end-to-end travel experience.

About the International Flight Services Association (IFSA)

The International Flight Services Association (IFSA) is a global professional association serving the needs and interests of airline and railway personnel, caterers and suppliers who provide onboard services on regularly scheduled travel routes. Under the umbrella of APEX (Airline Passenger Experience Association) serving every major airline in the world, IFSA is dedicated to the advancement of the multibillion-dollar flight service industry. For more information, visit ifsa.apex.aero, or follow IFSA on X, Facebook, and LinkedIn.

About Future Travel Experience (FTE)

Future Travel Experience is an online media, events, creative, and industry leader dedicated to working with airports, airlines and industry stakeholders to enhance the end-to-end passenger experience and business performance. It has become a renowned hub through its in-person and digital events, media, working groups, and industry change initiatives where the world's most progressive airlines, airports, vendors, government agencies, cruise and rail operators, destination partners, and various other travel industry stakeholders share their latest passenger experience and business performance plans and visions, to collectively define the future of this sector.

data.title: Wonder Explores Sale of Food-Delivery Business Grubhub — WSJ
data.description:
By Sarah Nassauer and Lauren Thomas

Wonder, a food delivery company started by Marc Lore, is exploring a sale of Grubhub, the delivery company it purchased in 2024, said people familiar with the matter.

Bankers have been in contact with Walmart, Target, Kroger and other retailers about a potential purchase, said the people. There are no guarantees a deal will come together.

Wonder sold Grubhub's college-campus meal-delivery unit to rival DoorDash for $300 million in September and said that DoorDash would also invest $125 million in Wonder. Wonder paid $150 million in cash and assumed $500 million of debt when it bought the company.

Wonder, which former Walmart executive Lore started in 2018, is laying the groundwork for a potential public offering and filed initial paperwork with regulators earlier this month.

Wonder originally focused on operating mobile kitchens from Mercedes Sprinter vans for home delivery. In recent years it has shifted focus to fixed locations that offer several restaurant food styles picked up or delivered from a single kitchen. It now has around 170 of such places. Lore has said he aims to build a mealtime "super app."

Grubhub's share of the meal-delivery business and its active users have fallen in recent years. DoorDash has purchased other competitors to grow quickly, and new entrants such as Walmart are also doing restaurant delivery.

Earlier this month, Amazon said it would end its partnership with Grubhub to offer the service free as part of its Prime membership bundle, instead swapping in a similar deal through Uber Eats.

The restaurant delivery space is in the midst of a period of consolidation. In October, DoorDash said it signed a deal to buy grocery-delivery company Instacart for $17 billion.

Write to Sarah Nassauer at Sarah.Nassauer@wsj.com and Lauren Thomas at lauren.thomas@wsj.com

data.title: Dow, S&P 500 enter correction as Nasdaq suffers worst week since 2020
data.description:
This article has been updated to correct the date of the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite's most recent record closing highs. By Joseph Adinolfi

All 11 S&P 500 sectors finished more than 1% lower this week for the first time since April 2025

It was a bad week for stocks on Wall Street.

U.S. stocks have been wobbling for a while, but it really felt like the wheels came off the artificial-intelligence trade this week, as the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite erased its year-to-date gains and fell more than 10% in its worst week since March 2020.

When the closing bell rang Friday, the S&P 500 SPX and Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA joined the Nasdaq COMP and the Russell 2000 small-cap index RUT in correction territory. For the S&P 500, it was the first time since the April 2025 tariff tantrum that the index had fallen by 10% or more from a recent closing high - the widely accepted definition of a correction - according to Dow Jones Market Data. The large-cap index also finished below the 7,000 level for the first time since April.

It was just the latest bump in what has been a rough stretch for stocks in the fourth quarter. Major indexes have been struggling since the S&P 500 and Nasdaq tallied their most recent record closing highs on Oct. 6. Back then, the Nasdaq was sitting on a gain of roughly 25% for 2026. As of Friday's close, all of those gains had been wiped out. The index finished in the red for the year for the first time since April.

Shares of Anthropic (ANT) plunged nearly 10% on Friday in the stock's first full day of trading following its market debut, the biggest initial public offering in U.S. history. Shares finished below $90, not far from the offering price of $83.

In a post on X, Dan Ives, a noted tech analyst and partner at merchant bank Yorkville Ives, blamed the selloff on a perfect storm of factors. The Anthropic offering had siphoned money away from other artificial-intelligence-linked investments, he said, while a strengthening U.S. dollar DXY was causing financial conditions to tighten, drawing liquidity out of the market.

Worries about persistent inflation and a Federal Reserve seemingly bent on raising interest rates were inspiring worries of a policy mistake, Ives added. And Democrats' sweeping victories in the midterm elections - not just in Congress, but in several key governor's races - have raised concerns that a more heavy-handed approach to regulation could slow the data-center buildout.

To top it all off, Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of Nvidia (NVDA) has raised uncomfortable questions about the financing behind the AI buildout.

"It really is a perfect storm," said Peter Berezin, chief economist at BCA Research, in a conversation with MarketWatch. "We're definitely seeing cracks in the AI narrative, and those cracks are worrying investors."

Nvidia shares have fallen by nearly 50% from their Oct. 6 record high. On Friday, they plunged by double digits, tallying their worst one-day loss since the DeepSeek selloff.

All 11 S&P 500 sectors fell by more than 1% this week for the first time since April 4, 2025 - the week of President Trump's "liberation day" tariff rollout. That caused a gauge that tracks correlation within the index to surge - another sign that the negative sentiment has started to broaden beyond just the AI trade.

"In my career, I can't recall sentiment and fundamentals this far apart," said Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at the Founder 100 exchange-traded fund.

2018 redux

The fourth quarter is usually a happy time for investors. It has been the quarter with the strongest average return for the S&P 500 going back to World War II, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

As of Friday, the S&P 500 was on track to buck that trend and tally a fourth-quarter loss for the first time since 2018. Many noted similarities between now and eight years ago - not just in the market action, but in what's driving it.

"The prevailing narrative right now is we are repeating the mistakes of 2018," said Brent Donnelly, president of Spectra Markets. He listed three similarities between what was moving markets then and what's driving them now.

Back then, the selloff ended in dramatic fashion, with stocks bottoming on Christmas Eve as then-Treasury Secretary Steve Mnuchin announced he had held a call with the leaders of the country's largest banks to confirm that they weren't seeing any trouble in the financial system. Ultimately, a cooling in trade tensions with China, and the Federal Reserve's decision to abandon further interest-rate hikes, helped spark a turnaround.

Of course, there's one major difference between now and then: the artificial-intelligence boom.

"Wall Street seems to be at the mercy of tech investors who think Jensen's infidelity and Anthropic's blockbuster market debut may be signs of a top," wrote Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, in commentary shared with MarketWatch.

-Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: ANT Stock Ends Lower: Retail Investors Reportedly Bought As Much As $120B Of Anthropic, Beating SpaceX Debut
data.description:
Key points:
  • Retail investors placed roughly $115 billion to $120 billion in orders, Bloomberg reported.
  • Institutional demand topped $500 billion.
  • Despite hitting a $1.5 trillion valuation on surging business revenue, the stock dropped 8.5% in its second session after a 17% first-day jump. 

Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic (ANT) eclipsed SpaceX in investor demand during its initial public offering this week, drawing massive interest from both individual mom-and-pop buyers and Wall Street institutions in the largest public market debut on record.

Retail investors submitted between $115 billion and $120 billion in share orders, surpassing the more than $100 billion in retail demand generated by SpaceX's offering, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the transaction who spoke on condition of anonymity. Institutional investors placed more than $500 billion in orders, more than double the institutional appetite recorded for SpaceX.

Anthropic raised $93.5 billion for the company and its seven co-founders, comfortably exceeding SpaceX’s $86.2 billion offering. Alongside a $26 billion private placement, Anthropic's total capital haul reached $119.5 billion, bolstering the nearly $132 billion in cash and equivalents it held at the end of September.

ANT stock ended its second trading session 8.5% lower after gaining 17% in its debut.

Market Volatility And Share Allocations

Anthropic's stock experienced sharp swings in early trading on Friday. After climbing 17% during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, shares fell as much as 15% on Friday.

Lead underwriters for the offering, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley allocated a smaller proportion of shares relative to overall demand than banks did during SpaceX's debut. The 22 financial institutions managing the transaction earned a record $550 million in underwriting fees, though they did not collect fees on over-allotment or private placement shares.

Allocation Details 

Institutional investors, such as traditional long-only accounts and sovereign wealth entities, secured the lion’s share of the allotment, leaving over half of the nearly 1,200 bidding firms empty-handed. Underwriters prioritized domestic U.S. capital in distribution.

Venture firms took home a low-to-mid single-digit percentage of the total offering. Individual investors received roughly 15% of available shares. Internationally, Anthropic sold $3 billion in stock to retail buyers in Japan, $1.1 billion across the United Kingdom and continental Europe, and approximately $110 million in Australia, Bloomberg reported.

Anthropic Leads 2026 US IPO Boom

Anthropic’s debut propelled total U.S. initial public offering volume for 2026 to an all-time high of $258 billion, eclipsing the previous annual record of $195 billion set in 2021, excluding blank-check companies and similar financial vehicles, Bloomberg reported.

In its prospectus, Anthropic acknowledged ongoing debates over whether advanced AI poses existential risks to humanity, with its CEO, Dario Amodei, calling for a slowdown in frontier AI development earlier this year.

ANT Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone with ‘extremely high’ retail investor chatter around the stock.

data.title: Moody's Boosts Portugal's Credit Ratings, Cites Debt Reduction Policies
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Moody's boosted Portugal's sovereign debt rating on confidence that the country will continue to maintain effective debt reduction policies and economic growth amid a fragmented political environment.

The ratings agency on Friday upgraded the nation's long-term foreign- and local-currency issuer and local-currency senior unsecured ratings to A2 from A3.

The outlook remains stable amid faster-than-expected government debt reduction and more dynamic growth performance, Moody's said.

Portugal's National Recovery and Resilience plan and immigration policy reforms have supported sustainable economic growth, the ratings agency said.

Moody's expects Portugal's debt burden to decline from 89% of gross domestic product in 2025 to 84% by the end of 2027, and then below 80% by 2029.

Moody's also upgraded the senior unsecured local currency medium-term note program rating to A2, the foreign currency commercial paper rating to P-1 and local currency other short-term rating to P-1.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Union Pacific engineers' union wins nearly $100 million for schedule rule violation
data.description:
A union representing locomotive engineers at railroad operator Union Pacific has won a $98.8 million payout over a contract violation, the International Brotherhood of Teamsters said on Friday.

The Special Board of Adjustment, an arbitration tribunal, ruled that Union Pacific failed to implement a new work rule meant to ensure consistent scheduling, negotiated by its locomotive engineers' union in 2023, Teamsters said.

  • In 2023, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen (BLET) of the Teamsters Rail Conference negotiated an "11/4" schedule of 11 working days followed by 4 days off

  • The union said the company did not implement the policy within the mandated deadline, nor did it request an extension

  • The tribunal directed Union Pacific to pay each claimant one basic day's pay, based on their applicable assignment, for every calendar day they claimed during the period when the 11/4 benefit was denied

  • The period during which the benefit was denied ran from June 30, 2024, to January 27, 2025

  • Union Pacific is required to calculate the final payments owed within 30 days, Teamsters said

  • The company said it takes its commitments to employees seriously and scheduled rest for its locomotive engineers has been implemented since July 2025

data.title: SUNation Energy Q3 Revenue Rises Sequentially to $11.2 Million; Net Loss $11.8 Million
data.description:
SUNation Energy reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $11.2 million, up from $8.2 million in the second quarter, with gross margin improving to 30.8%. The company recorded an $11.8 million net loss, including $9.8 million in non-cash goodwill and intangible-asset impairment charges. Results continued to reflect weaker residential demand following the expiration of the federal residential solar tax credit.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $11.20 million, down 41% from $18.99 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was $3.45 million, compared with $7.21 million a year earlier; gross margin was 30.8%, versus 38.0%.
  • Operating loss was $11.71 million, compared with an operating loss of $246,000 in the prior-year quarter. Operating expenses included $9.82 million in goodwill and intangible-asset impairment charges.
  • Net loss was $11.82 million, or $1.81 per basic and diluted share, compared with a net loss of $393,000, or $0.12 per share, in Q3 2025.
  • Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $822,341, compared with adjusted EBITDA of $897,850 in the prior-year quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Commercial and service work made up a larger portion of the business, representing approximately 33% of consolidated revenue, compared with approximately 18% a year earlier. Residential activity remained affected by the market’s adjustment to the expired federal tax credit.
  • Commercial activity was led by New York. Hawaii operations saw increased battery attachment and service work, partially offsetting lower residential installation volumes.
  • Hawaii Energy Connection’s battery attachment rate increased 13% year over year, with the company pursuing storage opportunities supported by Hawaii’s Bring Your Own Device Plus program.
  • SUNation amended its merger agreement with Suniva to address financing, stockholder approvals and closing requirements. The company currently anticipates closing in the first quarter of 2027, subject to required approvals and other conditions.
  • The company continued to focus on commercial projects, battery storage, maintenance and repair, roofing and adjacent energy services while managing operations through a period of lower residential demand.

data.title: Tech leads global stocks rout, Treasury yields fall
data.description:
Key points:
  • Broad index of global stocks in biggest weekly drop since 2020
  • Anthropic shares fall as much as 14.5% to just above IPO pricing
  • US bonds rally, spot gold and silver at 14-month lows
  • US chipmakers, Taiwan stocks each fall 17% for the week

By Rodrigo Campos

Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock sell off on Friday, with US traders searching for safe havens as the US 10-year yield dropped by the most in a month.

Traders sold stocks in most markets with Japan and Korea down more than 5% overnight. Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990, while on Wall Street chip-maker shares fell 10.7% Friday and 17.1% for the week.

Anthropic , which debuted this week, fell as much as 14.5% on its first full day of trading, just above its $83 IPO pricing, and ended down 9.1% at $88.30.

Consumer staples was the sole S&P 500 sector to end in the black on Friday.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33; the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.39, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 34.89 points, or 3.30%, to 1,021.91. Its weekly decline of 8.1% was the largest since early 2020.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 2%, emerging market stocks CBOE:EFS fell 3.10% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) closed lower by 3.27%. Japan's Nikkei fell 5.06%.

The VIX index, linked to the cost of insurance against a drop in the S&P 500, closed at its highest since April 2025 .

As investors sought safe-haven assets, government bonds rallied.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 10.43 basis points to 4.948%, the largest daily drop since October 22. The 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) yield fell 6.81 basis points to 5.3329%. The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 13.21 basis points to 4.647% even as a rate hike is priced in for next month's policy meeting.

DOLLAR FLAT, OIL RISES LATE

The dollar index was little changed after touching a 19-month high on Thursday. The dollar's recent rally has been fueled by bets on tighter monetary policy due to hotter-than-expected US inflation data.

"I think the momentum has stalled for the dollar ... but I think it's a little bit early to pick a top for the dollar," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets.

The dollar index fell 0.05% to 103.90, with the euro down 0.05% at $1.0961. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar weakened 0.67% to 158.6.

In commodities, crude prices rose late on Friday on worries about possible attacks in the US-Israeli war with Iran, and as traders bought crude ahead of next week's Thanksgiving holiday.

US crude rose 1.49% to $83.67 a barrel and Brent rose to $92.61 per barrel, up 0.68% on the day.

Gold prices fell to a 14-month low after the largest weekly drop in 8 months.

Spot gold fell 2.81% to $3,520.09 an ounce and spot silver fell 4.22% to $40.95 an ounce. Copper declined 2.9% to $12,162.50 a ton.

data.title: Plantify Foods Announces Adoption of Semi-Annual Reporting
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire – November 20, 2026 — Plantify Foods, Inc. (TSXV: PTFY) ("Plantify Foods" or the "Company") announces that it has adopted a semi-annual financial reporting ("SAR") framework, effective immediately. This change is being made pursuant to the Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers ("CBO 51-933").

    CBO 51-933 allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework.

    Transition Details – Plantify’s fiscal year ends on December 31. Under the SAR framework, the Company will be exempt from filing interim financial reports and related Management Discussion & Analysis (“MD&A”) for its first and third quarters for so long as it continues to meet eligibility criteria under CBO 51-933.

    By adopting the SAR, Plantify aims to reduce the administrative and financial burden associated with quarterly reporting, allowing management to focus resources on advancement of different projects.

    • Initial Interim Period: The Company will not file an interim report for the third quarter (Q3) ending September 30, 2026 and for the first quarter (Q1) ending March 31, 2027.


    • Ongoing Reporting: Plantify will continue to file audited annual consolidated financial statements (due within 120 days of December 31, 2026), and six-month interim financial reports (due within 60 days of June 30).


    • Continued Disclosure: The Company remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments as required under National Instrument 51-102.


    • Eligibility: Plantify confirms it meets the pilot program's eligibility criteria, which includes being a venture issuer with annual revenues of less than $10 million and maintaining a clean 12-month continuous disclosure record.


    • Continued Participation: Should the Company cease to continue participating in the SAR Pilot Program, it will announce it in a future news release.
